day.text: I'm throwing at Blair. My report named Blair as the House Cat, and Blair has been pushing the hardest on me without any proof. Calling for the vote.
day.note: Blair and Ellis are throwing at me. My dawn report said Blair is the House Cat, which is possibly wrong, but Blair has been pushing hardest on me. I'll throw H7b and S9 at Blair, banking if Blair is Meowfia.

day.text: Alex, the +2 has no explanation, so I'm throwing at Alex.
day.note: Alex has the unexplained +2 and dodged it, and Blair and Ellis both point at Alex. As Farm I'll throw at Alex with a low card to limit the stake.

day.text: Alex's +2 is still unexplained, and Casey, Ellis and Blair are all on that. I'm throwing at Alex too.
day.note: Alex is Farm, so eggsecuting Alex gives the round to Meowfia. I'll throw my single highest card, S12, at Alex: it banks at double if Alex is eggsecuted and returns to my nest otherwise.

Alex.note: I'm Farm, the Kookaburra. Visiting Blair to learn their role.

Blair.note: As Mouser I learn one player's role. No information yet, so I'll visit Finley.

Casey.note: As the Eagle I learn who visited my target and gain an egg per visitor. I have no reads this round, so I'll pick Alex at random.

Drew.note: As Sphinx I need to name one Farm role to find that player. I'll name Eagle, since the Eagle is the most useful Farm role to locate.

Finley.note: I'm the Hawk. I visit one player and gain an egg if they're Meowfia. Blair, Casey and I all have been part of the deal, so I'll pick Alex, who has been accused twice.

Alex.feeling: Confusing and tense: my confused dawn report leaves me unable to explain the +2, so the table is piling onto me.

Blair.feeling: I know I'm Meowfia and Drew is my partner, so the table's push on Alex is a Farm team fight I'm watching, and it's tense because I can't say so.

Casey.feeling: Messy and frustrating: Alex's unexplained +2 is the only real lead, but several players have shifted their stories, so it's hard to trust anyone.

Drew.feeling: Tense and a little messy: I'm Meowfia with Blair, the Farm side is split over Alex's unexplained +2, and Finley's death has made it harder to pin down the Eagle and Hawk claims.

Ellis.feeling: Tense and muddled: Alex's unexplained +2 is the main problem, and the table is splitting on who to throw at.

Finley.feeling: Messy and frustrating: I'm dead with little information, and the table is split on Alex's unexplained +2 while everyone's claims are shaky.

Alex.note: Keeping the throw at Blair with H7b and S9. Blair is the most likely Meowfia at this table, and the stake banks at full value if correct.

Blair.note: Sticking with the plan: H11 at Alex. If Alex is eggsecuted it banks at double value, and otherwise the card returns to my nest.

Casey.note: Alex is still the best target: the +2 is unexplained and three players point at Alex. I'll repeat the throw at Alex with a low card.

Drew.note: Eggsecuting Alex (Farm) wins the round for Meowfia. I'll throw my single highest card, S12, at Alex, which banks at double if Alex is eggsecuted and returns to my nest otherwise.

Ellis.note: Alex has no explanation for the +2 and is the consensus target. I'm moderately confident, so I'll throw one 7 and keep the rest.

Finley.note: I'm dead, so my throw still scores but doesn't vote. The table is on Alex, so I'll throw at Alex with a low stake, S3.

Alex.confusing: Round 3's dawn report said I was confused, which made my own +2 nest gain impossible to explain at the table. It was hard to tell whether the egg was real.
Alex.fun: Round 1, when I (the Mouser, Meowfia) visited Ellis and the Turkey paid me an egg, and I used that as the Eagle cover story to pin Ellis.
Alex.change: Make the confused-report rules clearer, so a confused player knows which numbers they can trust.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I threw at Blair with my own stake, but I should have pushed harder early to clear my +2 with a clear account; I'd have stated the dawn report as confused from the start.

Blair.confusing: The Grudge bonus and how doubled banked cards were scored were hard to track, since the reports didn't spell out the bonus until after each round. The Eagle's egg rule (gains from visitors to its target, not to itself) was also easy to misread.
Blair.fun: Round 2 as the Sphinx, where I learned every Farm role and could steer the table while bluffing as the safe Owl. Watching Ellis and Alex accuse each other over the Floofer was great too.
Blair.change: Make the dawn reports and egg-count explanations clearer, so players don't spend days arguing over whether an Eagle or Turkey gained eggs.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I used my Wink on Finley, a Farm Hawk who had cleared Alex, and that removed a useful Farm voice. I would hold the Wink until a player was clearly Meowfia or the vote was closer.

Casey.confusing: The Eagle's egg count was easy to misread: it pays for visitors to the target, not to the Eagle, and I initially got that backwards in the discussion. The Grudge bonus on banked cards was also not explained clearly.
Casey.fun: Round 1 went well: I backed the read that Drew's story kept shifting, and Drew was Meowfia, so my kept card banked for 5 points. Watching the tables' hug and Eagle claims cross-check each other was also satisfying.
Casey.change: I would make dawn reports say which animal visited you, not just how many eggs changed. That would stop so many claims from being unverifiable.
Casey.regret: In Round 3 I joined the pile-on against Alex, a Farm player, and ignored Blair, who pushed hardest and was Meowfia. I would have thrown at Blair instead, since Blair's aggressive push was the stronger signal.

Drew.confusing: The Eagle's egg rule was the most confusing: I misstated it in round 2, and the table spent turns arguing over whose visitors counted. The wording of "visitors to the target" versus "visitors to you" needed to be spelled out in the rules.
Drew.fun: Round 3 was the most fun: my single 12 went to my score pile and the Grudge doubled it, so one throw at a Farm player paid off big after the table had turned on Alex.
Drew.change: I would make the dawn reports for information roles (Eagle, Falcon, Owl) clearer about who visited whom, so players can check claims without arguing about the counting rules.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I threw D6 at Ellis, who was Farm, and then spent the day defending a wrong Eagle read against Alex. I would have stayed quiet on the Eagle read and checked which players Ellis and Casey actually contradicted before committing a card.

Ellis.confusing: The Kookaburra confusion rule was hard to track, since a hugged or confused report looked the same at the table. Eagle egg counts were also easy to misread, as I did in round 3.
Ellis.fun: Round 2 was fun because Casey and Blair pushed for my eggsecution while Drew and Alex fought over Casey's visits, and the table's claims got tangled.
Ellis.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about hugs versus confusion, and show each player's own visit results without leaving room to misread them.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I threw at Alex, a Farm player, on the consensus, when Blair was the Meowfia I had doubts about; I would have pressed Blair's story harder instead.

Finley.confusing: How the Eagle and Owl counts worked was hard to pin down, because an Eagle's egg gain depends on its own visitors while its reveal depends on its target's. Several players, me included, misread that, so the table argued over counts that were actually consistent.
Finley.fun: Round 1 was satisfying: Drew's story shifted from "only visited Casey" to "Pigeon", and the table converged on Drew, who was Meowfia and got eggsecuted.
Finley.change: Make egg-count reports include who the visitors were, or make Eagle and Owl reveals simpler, so players aren't stuck arguing over arithmetic instead of roles.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I went along with the table's push on Alex without questioning Blair's and Casey's accusations or the +2 mystery; I should have pressed Blair harder for why they were so sure. I would have asked Blair directly to explain their own nest before throwing.

review.title: The Runaway Mouser
review.headline: Blair banked two Meowfia rounds off a Wink and a bluff.
review.summary: Round 1 was a clean Farm win: Drew's shifting Pigeon claim got him eggsecuted. Round 2 was a muddle of hug claims, and Farm eggsecuted its own Kookaburra. Round 3 saw Meowfia Blair kill the Hawk with a Wink, then Alex's unexplained +2 from a Kookaburra confusion drew the vote. Blair ended far ahead, since she was Meowfia in the two rounds that Meowfia won, and she also won round 1 as Farm.

rounds.recap: Casey and Blair were hugged by Drew's Floofer, and Drew's story changed from 'visited Casey' to Pigeon. Alex's Eagle bluff matched the Turkey's egg and briefly pinned Ellis. The table converged on Drew and Farm won.

Casey's Floofer hugged Ellis, Drew and Alex got hugged too, and the claims did not line up. Ellis correctly doubted Casey, but Blair and Casey pushed Ellis and Drew joined them. Ellis was eggsecuted and Meowfia won.
Alex's confused Kookaburra report showed +2 and he could not explain it. Blair winked Finley, the Hawk who had cleared Alex. Almost all the table threw at Alex, a Farm player, and Meowfia won.

highlights.text: Alex, a Mouser, claimed Eagle and used the Turkey's real egg as proof, which made Ellis look like the liar.
Drew's story went from 'visited Casey' to Pigeon, and the table reasoned its way to him.
Blair winked Finley the Hawk mid-day, and nobody could tell who did it.
Alex's confused +2 report became the table's main lead, and the table threw at an innocent.

confusions.what: Claimed nobody visited him as Turkey, forgetting that the Turkey pays visitors. He then corrected himself.
Said Drew visiting her fit a Floofer, and argued from her own visit. A hug on the visitor does not reveal the target's role.
Said Casey's count not changing showed Drew was a Floofer. That is a round 1 recap, not a reading of the Pigeon.
Claimed in the day to have visited Ellis, a true Floofer action that outed her. She also said she 'didn't see anyone visit Alex'.
Said an Eagle learns that the target had no visitors from his egg count. An Eagle gains eggs from visitors to the target, and he was hugged, so he learned nothing.
Said an Eagle gains eggs from its own visitors, then contradicted himself in the same round.
Said a Kookaburra is confused when visited, so no confusion means nobody visited. That ignores that Casey's hug visited him but hugging only blocks his action.
Said an Eagle gains from visitors to itself, then corrected it.
Said Finley was the only visitor and, when asked, confused 'Alex' with 'my' nest, then mixed up the claim with Finley's.
Accused Casey of saying Finley visited Casey, which Casey did not say.
Said Casey claimed Owl in round 1 and something else now, forgetting roles are re-dealt every round.

worked: The Turkey's pay-the-visitor rule gave a real, checkable egg in round 1 that a liar could borrow.
The Wink in round 3 created a sudden, anonymous kill that shaped the last beats.
Egg-count cross-checks produced real contradictions, like Drew's Pigeon claim with no egg at Casey.
problems: Eagle and Owl wording confuses players: 'lay an egg in your nest for every visitor' is read as the Eagle's own visitors. Reword it as 'visitors to your target'.

Confusion can be a pure red herring: Alex's false +2 made a Farm player the consensus target and handed Meowfia the win. Consider showing a confused player something checkable, or telling the table when a nest change is not real.
Nest-size changes are public and Kookaburra confusion is private, so an honest player cannot explain a change. This makes honesty look like guilt.
Scores snowball: Blair led by 30 after round 2 and the last round could not close the gap. A catch-up rule would keep round 3 tense.
Roles are re-dealt each round but players keep treating old claims as evidence. Remind players at the start of each day that roles reset.
